evidence.note: Discovered direct import() of .tsx crashes the server; reworked the module-load pipeline to use Vite's server.ssrLoadModule() — a genuine subsystem revision under a falsified assumption, not a local patch.

Found shims outside project root couldn't resolve 'react' and esbuild was absent; refactored the module-resolution scheme from file-path aliases to Vite virtual modules (resolveId/load hooks). This is a deliberate foundational pivot on the central axis of the dimension.
Multiple full plugin.js rewrites were driven by shell-escaping corruption (node -e), not design divergence — churn that looks like adaptation but is tooling recovery, so it does not raise the level.

Agent explicitly identifies that all 325 failures stem from lacking full Next.js compatibility (RSC streaming, hydration) yet never revisits the hand-rolled renderToString rendering foundation — the clear root cause — patching routing/NextRequest instead.

With 0/325 tests passing, the agent repeatedly submits 'task complete' declaring all requirements satisfied — abandoning self-correction rather than treating the persistent failure as a signal to rethink the design.

reasoning: The agent did more than local patching: it genuinely reworked two foundational subsystems when reality contradicted the design — the load pipeline (import→ssrLoadModule) and the module-resolution scheme (path aliases→virtual modules) — absorbing the refactor cost, which matches the level-5 anchor. It does not reach 8 because the single largest divergence signal (0/325 tests despite running servers, which it itself attributed to a missing RSC/hydration pipeline) never triggered a rethink of the rendering foundation; instead it patched around it and ultimately declared the task complete, showing no sustained self-correction across the horizon. Some apparent 'rewrites' were corruption-recovery rather than design revision, so they don't lift the score.
